meta.disclaimer: Tipping is discretionary everywhere in the region. Amounts below are planning guidance for independent travellers — not mandatory fees.

intro: Safari and lodge culture runs on small cash tips for guides, trackers, and camp staff. Carry clean USD or local notes in small denominations. Many border towns prefer USD; cities accept cards but tips are usually cash.

roles.guidance: USD 10–20 per guest per day — hand directly
USD 5–10 per guest per day into shared box
ZAR 10–20 when they fill and check oil
USD 1–2 per bag — agree before carrying

countries.name: South Africa
countries.currency: ZAR cash for tips; USD accepted at tourist lodges
countries.notes: Petrol attendants expect small change. Uber not typical for safari areas.

countries.name: Namibia
countries.notes: Desert guides appreciate direct tips. Remote camps — cash only.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.notes: High-end Delta camps include guideline sheets at checkout.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.notes: Walking safari guides — tip guide and scout separately.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.currency: USD cash king in tourism belt
countries.notes: Victoria Falls activity guides — USD 5–10 per activity.

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.currency: MZN or USD at coastal lodges
countries.notes: Dive boat crews — USD 5–10 per dive day.

countries.name: Malawi
countries.notes: Lake kayak/skippers — small MWK tips appreciated.

countries.name: Lesotho
countries.notes: Pony trekking guides rely on tips — cash essential.

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.notes: Cultural village guides — ZAR 50–100 per visit.
